name: Kim Gordon
label: Matador
lede: Kim Gordon had never played an instrument when she joined her first band at 27. She went on to co-found Sonic Youth, and at 70 she made a record on trap beats that Pitchfork ranked No. 10 for 2024.

eras.title: Art school first, by accident the rest
eras.text: She grew up in Rochester and Los Angeles and trained as a visual artist. In 1980 she reached New York to make art, wrote for Artforum, and drifted into the downtown noise scene without planning to.

years.h: Kim Gordon finishes art school with no band in sight
years.p: Her BFA comes from Otis College of Art and Design, after a short stretch working for the dealer Larry Gagosian.
years.xp: Born in Rochester in 1953, Gordon moved to Los Angeles at five when her father took a professorship at UCLA. She did two years at Santa Monica College, tried York University in Toronto and left homesick, then finished at Otis College of Art and Design.

years.h: She moves to New York for the art, not the music
years.p: Gordon writes for Artforum and starts Design Office, a project of interventions in friends' apartments.
years.xp: In 1981 she curated a show at White Columns gallery with work by Mike Kelley and Tony Oursler. The gallery would matter again within months: it hosted the Noise Fest where Sonic Youth first played.

eras.title: A bass at 27, and no drummer
eras.text: Gordon started with CKM, then formed Sonic Youth with Thurston Moore and Lee Ranaldo. It took four years and three drummers to find the sound.

years.h: At 27, Gordon joins CKM without ever having played
years.p: Through bandmate Stanton Miranda she meets Lee Ranaldo and Thurston Moore, and starts dating Moore.
years.xp: CKM was short-lived: Gordon, Christine Hahn and Stanton Miranda. It was the first time Gordon had picked up an instrument, and it led straight to the two guitarists she'd start Sonic Youth with.

years.h: Sonic Youth plays Noise Fest at White Columns
years.p: Gordon, Moore and Ranaldo do three songs with no drummer, in the gallery where Gordon had curated a show that year. Ranaldo is also playing in Glenn Branca's guitar ensemble.
years.xp:
The name came together in mid-1981: Fred "Sonic" Smith of the MC5 plus the reggae artist Big Youth.

Richard Edson drummed first (1981 to 1982), then [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] (1982 to 1985).

years.h: Glenn Branca signs Sonic Youth to Neutral Records
years.p: Neutral puts out the self-titled 1982 EP, their first record, to good reviews and almost no distribution.

years.h: Confusion Is Sex and a live Stooges cover
years.p: Gordon sings, plays bass and guitar and co-produces the band's first album, with Bob Bert on drums.
years.xp: Critics split: Entertainment Weekly's Chuck Eddy later called it the band's funniest, hardest-rocking and most underrated album, while the Chicago Tribune's Greg Kot said the noise-guitar revolution fell flat on tape.

years.h: Gordon and Moore get married
years.p: The marriage runs 27 years, through every Sonic Youth record and tour.

years.h: Drummer number three, Steve Shelley, settles it
years.p: After Richard Edson and Bob Bert, Shelley completes the lineup of Gordon, Moore, Ranaldo and Shelley. It doesn't change until the end.

eras.title: SST takes them national, then a double album
eras.text: A 1986 deal with SST took the band national. By the end of the decade Gordon had co-written a double album that critics ranked second of 1988, and she was already running side projects.

years.cap: Sonic Youth in a 1987 publicity photo for SST
years.h: Sister turns Philip K. Dick into a record
years.p: Cut on analog gear at Sear Sound in Manhattan over March and April 1987, a loose concept album with SST's name on the label.
years.xp: The opener Schizophrenia was originally titled Sister. Wikipedia reports that Gordon's own brother's schizophrenia partly inspired it. Pitchfork later ranked the record 14th on its best albums of the 1980s.

years.h: A 1983 Gerhard Richter candle fronts Daydream Nation
years.p: Recorded July and August 1988 at Greene St. Recording in Manhattan, with Gordon singing The Sprawl and Kissability.
years.xp: The cover is Richter's painting Kerze (Candle). NME gave the album a perfect score, Rolling Stone ranked it second of 1988, and the Village Voice's Pazz and Jop poll also put it second. The Library of Congress later chose it for the National Recording Registry.

eras.title: A major label and a crowded calendar
eras.text: Sonic Youth went to Geffen for Goo, toured with Nirvana and headlined Lollapalooza. Gordon also produced Hole, started Free Kitten, launched a clothing line and raised a daughter.

years.h: Geffen signs Sonic Youth for five albums and $300,000
years.p: The deal moves the band to Geffen's DGC label and comes with creative control.

years.h: Gordon interviews LL Cool J, then writes "Kool Thing"
years.p: Goo gives Sonic Youth its first commercial hit. Chuck D of Public Enemy speaks on the single and appears in the video.
years.xp:
The "Kool Thing" video (June 4, 1990, directed by Tamra Davis) was the band's first for a major label. Gordon wanted to wear a beret and carry an Uzi as a "poseur-leftist"; Geffen vetoed it. The single reached No. 7 on Billboard's modern rock chart.

Gordon also wrote Tunic (Song for Yaryus) for the album, about Karen Carpenter.

years.h: Gordon and Don Fleming make Hole's debut in a week
years.p: Four days recording and three mixing at Music Box Studios in Hollywood. [[Courtney Love|31d2041c-985d-48f7-b6e2-2a70cdf14853]] had pursued Gordon for the job with a letter and a Hello Kitty barrette.
years.xp: Gordon said Love "was either charming and nice or screaming at her band", but rated her as a singer and front person. Pretty on the Inside came out September 17, 1991 on Caroline.

years.h: Sonic Youth goes to Europe with Nirvana and a film crew
years.p: The 1991 tour also carries Dinosaur Jr., Babes in Toyland, Gumball and Mudhoney. The documentary, 1991: The Year Punk Broke, comes out in 1992.
years.xp: The title nods to the year Nirvana's Nevermind arrived.

years.src: Wikipedia: Free Kitten · Stereogum: We've Got
years.h: Gordon and Julia Cafritz start a band called Kitten
years.p: Lawyers for a heavy metal singer object to the name, and it becomes [[Free Kitten|7e623dd5-bf40-4f8b-ba71-8226afc918e2]].
years.xp: Gordon says she and Cafritz started the band inspired by Royal Trux. Yoshimi P-We of the Boredoms later played drums and [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]] of Pavement played bass, and the band played Lollapalooza in 1993. Albums: Nice Ass (1995) and Sentimental Education (1997) on Kill Rock Stars.

years.h: Gordon and Spike Jonze direct The Breeders' "Cannonball"
years.p: The same year she and Daisy von Furth launch the X-Girl clothing line.
years.xp: X-Girl grew out of X-Large, co-founded by the Beastie Boys' Mike D; the first store opened in 1994 and Chloe Sevigny modeled for it. Gordon sold her share in 1999.

years.h: Coco Hayley Moore is born
years.p: The daughter of Gordon and Moore arrives in 1994; the family moves to Northampton, Massachusetts in 1999.

years.h: Sonic Youth headlines Lollapalooza, with Hole and Pavement on the bill
years.p: Fourteen years after a gallery set with no drummer, the band tops a touring festival.

years.h: Thieves take nearly 30 Sonic Youth guitars from a tour van
years.p: The instruments disappear in Orange County, California.

eras.title: One last album, then the marriage ends
eras.text: Sonic Youth's final album came out on Matador. Two years later Gordon and Moore separated and the band ended.

years.cap: Gordon with Sonic Youth at Rock en Seine, Paris
years.h: The last Sonic Youth album goes to Matador
years.p: The Eternal is the band's final record. Matador also releases everything Gordon makes on her own afterward.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kim Gordon · Stereogum: We've Got
years.h: 27 years in, Gordon and Moore announce they're separating
years.p: The band plays its final show on November 14, 2011 in Brazil. Gordon later writes that Moore had an affair; the divorce is finalized in April 2013.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports Gordon's account, given in her memoir and interviews. Asked in 2024 about the final show at Brazil's SWU festival, she said she talked about it in her book and does not think about it much anymore.

eras.title: Life after the band
eras.text: With Sonic Youth over, Gordon started an experimental duo in Northampton, wrote a memoir and moved back to Los Angeles.

years.cap: Body/Head, Gordon and Bill Nace, at Supersonic festival, Birmingham, October 2012
years.h: Gordon and Bill Nace take two guitars on the road as Body/Head
years.p: She forms the duo with Nace in Northampton around 2011. No drummer, a lot of effects pedals.
years.xp: The name comes from a book about the films of Catherine Breillat. Early shows projected slowed-down film footage behind two guitars and Gordon's voice.

q: It's almost like a Cassavetes film or something.
years.h: Coming Apart sorts hours of playing into a double album
years.p: Mostly improvised guitar and vocals, picked from long sessions by Gordon and Nace.
years.xp: Gordon said they played a lot together, then went through and picked the pieces. She said it is not the same as jamming.

years.h: Gordon writes Girl in a Band without a co-writer
years.p: Dey Street Books publishes the memoir of her childhood, Sonic Youth, and the marriage and its end.
years.xp: Questlove reviewed it in the New York Times, praising its introspection and real feeling; NME called it a record of 50 years of alternative culture. The Guardian felt it was reductive on the marriage's end.

eras.title: Trap beats at 70
eras.text: Gordon's solo records, made with the producer Justin Raisen, pair her voice with hip-hop rhythms. The second, The Collective, earned her first Grammy nominations.

years.h: Thirty-eight years in, Gordon makes a solo album
years.p: She meets producer [[Justin Raisen|88728e3a-1dd6-4db4-a21f-d67d8d3dd5c0]] through an Airbnb rental, which also gives a song its title, Air BnB.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.4; the Guardian's Laura Snapes gave it a perfect score.

years.big: "I picked something really mundane, like a packing list, just to contrast it."
years.h: "Bye Bye" puts a packing list over an 808
years.p: Gordon on the lyric. Raisen built the beat for trap; Stereogum says it was originally made for Playboi Carti. Her daughter Coco is in the video.

years.cap: Kim Gordon on her 2024 solo tour
years.src: Wikipedia: The Collective · Year-End Lists · ABC · Paste
years.h: Pitchfork ranks The Collective No. 10 of 2024
years.p: Shaad D'Souza gives it 8.5 in the review; Metacritic scores it 84.
years.xp:
Gordon said Raisen sent beats and she decided which she could do something on, then added guitar and made up vocals. She told the ABC she works off rhythm better than melody. The title comes from the collective consciousness in Jennifer Egan's novel The Candy House, and Rachel Kushner supplied phrases for lyrics.

The album got two Grammy nominations (Best Alternative Music Album and, for "Bye Bye", Best Alternative Music Performance), her first.

years.h: Gordon takes the trap-beat songs to Glastonbury
years.p: BBC Music films the set.

years.h: Gordon rewrites "Bye Bye" for the Trump administration
years.p: The new version, "BYE BYE 25!", comes out in mid-2025 with updated lyrics.

years.h: Dave Grohl drums on "Busy Bee"
years.p: Play Me is Gordon's third solo album, again produced by Raisen. The song samples Gordon and [[Julia Cafritz|b99fc6af-0753-4f0a-832f-615d9e61394c]] on a 1990s MTV beach house.
